the development of novel high-performance real-time systolic architectures for 2D HR spatio-temporal filters that are capable of GHz frame-rates, thereby facilitating the implementation of high-speed RF smart antenna applications.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the work presented in this thesis represents a significant contribution to the field of 2D real-time spatio/temporal digital filters.
the work presented in this thesis has resulted in a real-time systolic-array processor implementation of two dimensional IIR filters for RF smart-antenna applications.
the proposed systolic-array architecture has been successfully implemented in a real-time FPGA prototype, and that the prototype achieves the required OFPCC frame-rates for RF smart antennas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2D HR filter architecture proposed in this thesis is the fastest 2D HR IIR filter architecture in the literature.
the proposed architecture and method is capable of real-time 2D I IR filtering at high throughput, which is suitable for RF smart antenna arrays.
the proposed architecture is capable of real-time OFP CC 2D I IR filtering of temporally downconverted RF signals at a clock frequency in excess of 100 MHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed 2D LA systolic-array architecture has the potential to be used in high-speed RF smart-antenna applications, where 2D IHR filtering is required.
the proposed architecture is capable of high through put, low critical path delays and low power consumption.
a novel systolic-array implementation of 2D IHR filters can be achieved with low critical path delays, high throughputs, low area and low power.
